purpose: This deliverable crosses Business Value against Technical Complexity to provide a prioritization signal, not a cancellation verdict. Its objective is to prevent a team from investing 6 months in a problem that delivers little value or is too complex for the current budget.
inputs:
| Artifact | Use | Consumed in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[example_output_impact_estimate]] | Frequency and estimated Annual Impact (P0-D3), to be converted into Severity/Scale. | Step 1 |
| [[example_output_problem_classification]] | Dominant Archetype and non-binding Remedy (P0-D2), to estimate engineering effort. | Step 2 |

steps.title: Evaluate Business Value
steps.summary: Convert D3 Frequency and Annual Impact into a Business Value classification (High/Medium/Low) through explicit thresholds, not subjective impressions.

substeps.title: Conversion to Factual Severity
substeps.objective: Translate Downstream Effect into one of 5 factual categories, prohibiting emotional descriptions.
substeps.input: - D1 Derived Effect and D3 Estimated Annual Impact (9,600,000 COP/year).
substeps.raw_data: Forced refunds with bank fee absorption, lost commissions, client grievance claims. Annualized loss: 9,600,000 COP/year.

micro.title: Classification on fixed scale
micro.objective: Select the highest factual severity category sustained by D3 evidence.

steps: Review the 5 fixed factual categories: Inconvenience < Time Lost < Task Blocked < Financial Loss < Safety Risk.
Filter out emotional terms ('frustrating', 'annoying', 'chaotic') and probe the concrete damage.
Match documented facts: forced refunds and lost commissions represent direct monetary loss.
Assign Financial Loss as the verified severity category.
how_to.table_columns: Severity Category | Category Definition | Evidence Match | Classified Status
how_to.table_rules: One row showing the highest substantiated severity level.
restrictions: Choose the highest category evidence supports.

micro.example:
| Severity Category | Category Definition | Evidence Match | Classified Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| **Financial Loss** | Direct monetary loss, absorbed transaction surcharges, and lost revenue | D3 documents 9,600,000 COP/year in refunds, bank fees, and lost commissions | **`CLASSIFIED`** |

*Rule Check:* Prohibited emotional terms avoided; classification rests strictly on monetary records.

substeps.title: Evaluation against the Three Threshold Criteria
substeps.objective: Activate Business Value only if the problem crosses at least one of the three objective criteria (A, B, or C).
substeps.raw_data:
Criterion A: Daily/weekly frequency + Task Blocked or worse.
Criterion B: Multi-unit scale + Time Lost or worse.
Criterion C: Financial Loss or Safety Risk regardless of frequency.

micro.title: Criterion A (Chronic Failure)
micro.objective: Test problem against Criterion A threshold.

steps: Check frequency requirement: daily or weekly occurrence.
Check severity requirement: Task Blocked or worse.
Compare case data: frequency is monthly (12/year), not daily/weekly.
Mark Criterion A as NO.
how_to.table_columns: Criterion | Condition | Met? | Supporting Evidence from D3

micro.example:
| Criterion | Condition | Met? | Supporting Evidence from D3 |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **A — Chronic Failure** | Daily/Weekly frequency + Blocked Task or worse | `NO` | Frequency is monthly (12/year), not daily or weekly. |
micro.link_label: Criterion A result goes to B (1.2.2)

micro.title: Criterion B (Death by a Thousand Cuts)
micro.objective: Test problem against Criterion B threshold.

steps: Check scale requirement: operational spread across multiple units, properties, or shifts.
Check severity requirement: Time Lost or worse.
Compare case data: double bookings affect individual properties per event, not simultaneous fleet-wide operations.
Mark Criterion B as NO.
how_to.table_columns: Criterion | Condition | Met? | Supporting Evidence from D3
how_to.table_rules: Rows showing Criterion A and B progress.

micro.example:
| Criterion | Condition | Met? | Supporting Evidence from D3 |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **A — Chronic Failure** | Daily/Weekly frequency + Blocked Task or worse | `NO` | Frequency is monthly (12/year), not daily or weekly. |
| **B — Death by a Thousand Cuts** | Multi-unit scale + Time Lost or worse | `NO` | Impacts individual properties per event, not operations across multiple business units simultaneously. |
micro.link_label: Criteria A & B go to C (1.2.3)

micro.title: Criterion C (Catastrophic Failure)
micro.objective: Test problem against Criterion C threshold.

steps: Check condition: Severity is Financial Loss or Safety Risk, regardless of frequency.
Compare case data: verified severity is Financial Loss (9,600,000 COP/year).
Mark Criterion C as YES.
Issue consolidated Threshold Table.
how_to.table_columns: Criterion | Condition | Met? | Supporting Evidence from D3
how_to.table_rules: Complete table covering all 3 threshold criteria.
restrictions: Criterion C activates regardless of event frequency.
how_to.done_when: Threshold Table complete with Criterion C activation.

micro.example:
| Criterion | Condition | Met? | Supporting Evidence from D3 |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **A — Chronic Failure** | Daily/Weekly frequency + Blocked Task or worse | `NO` | Frequency is monthly (12/year), not daily/weekly. |
| **B — Death by a Thousand Cuts** | Multi-unit + Lost Time or worse | `NO` | Impacts individual properties per event, not operations across multiple business units simultaneously. |
| **C — Catastrophic Failure** | Financial Loss or Security Risk, regardless of frequency | **`YES`** | Annual Impact of 9,600,000 COP in direct financial losses (refunds + lost commissions), documented in D3. |

substeps.title: Business Value Derivation
substeps.objective: Apply the derivation rule to declare High, Medium, or Low Business Value.
substeps.input: - Threshold table from 1.2: Criterion C = YES.
substeps.raw_data: Criterion C met -> HIGH. Only A/B met -> MEDIUM. None met -> LOW.

micro.title: Business value derivation rule
micro.objective: Derive Business Value level based on active threshold criteria and verify confidence caveats.

steps: Apply derivation rule: Criterion C is YES -> Business Value is HIGH.
Check D3 Confidence Level: D3 is Medium, so low-certainty warning caveats do not trigger.
Formulate Business Value declaration stating Criterion C activation.
how_to.table_columns: Evaluation Axis | Active Criterion | Resulting Value | Confidence Status
how_to.table_rules: One row declaring final Business Value.
restrictions: A catastrophic failure is High value regardless of low frequency.

micro.example:
| Evaluation Axis | Active Criterion | Resulting Value | Confidence Status |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Business Value** | **Criterion C** (Financial Loss) | **`HIGH`** | Solid: D3 confidence is Medium; no low-certainty override applies. |

*Rule Confirmation:* Criterion C triggers HIGH value; monetary loss justifies high engineering prioritization.

steps.title: Evaluate Technical Complexity
steps.summary: Estimate engineering effort based on the non-binding signal from D2, without committing to architectural design.

substeps.title: Complexity Mapping by Archetype
substeps.input:
- Dominant Archetype: Information Asymmetry.
- Theoretical Pattern: Single Source of Truth with concurrency control.
substeps.raw_data: Information Asymmetry / Workflow: typically MEDIUM. Integration Disconnect: MEDIUM-HIGH. Algorithmic: HIGH.

micro.title: Indicative complexity mapping
micro.objective: Map Information Asymmetry to standard complexity baseline and check upward adjustment factors.

steps: Look up Information Asymmetry in indicative guide: baseline is MEDIUM.
Check upward adjustment conditions: multiple legacy integrations, hardware, frontier AI.
Verify absence of upward adjustment factors in D2 Technical Focus.
Assign MEDIUM technical complexity baseline.
how_to.table_columns: Archetype | Standard Baseline | Adjustment Factors | Resulting Complexity
how_to.table_rules: One row evaluating archetype technical complexity.
restrictions: Complexity mapping is an orientation, not a binding architectural decision.
Upward adjustments require explicit evidence of hardware or complex APIs.

micro.example:
| Archetype | Standard Baseline | Adjustment Factors | Resulting Complexity |
| :--- | :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **Information Asymmetry** | `MEDIUM` | None: D2 mentions zero hardware, legacy mainframe integrations, or frontier AI. | **`MEDIUM`** |

*Rationale:* Concurrency control and consistency are addressed through well-known transactional database patterns.

substeps.title: Explicit Justification
substeps.objective: Draft concrete justification linking complexity rating directly to D2's Technical Focus.
substeps.raw_data: Single source of truth and instant inquiry mechanism with concurrency control.

micro.title: Technical focus alignment
micro.objective: Publish formal justification connecting MEDIUM complexity with standard transactional patterns.

steps: Reference D2 Technical Focus verbatim.
Explain why standard transactional mechanisms keep complexity at MEDIUM.
Confirm that no frontier R&D is required.
how_to.table_columns: Evaluation Axis | Complexity Level | Direct Justification

micro.example:
| Evaluation Axis | Complexity Level | Direct Justification |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Technical Complexity** | **`MEDIUM`** | "The technical focus demands concurrency control and real-time availability inquiry, resolvable through standard transactional patterns; it does not require frontier algorithms, legacy integrations, or hardware." |

steps.title: Matrix Placement, Human Confirmation, and Continuity Signal
steps.summary: Intersect Value (HIGH) and Complexity (MEDIUM), obtain human confirmation of the verdict, and issue the continuity signal.

substeps.title: Cross and Quadrant
substeps.objective: Intersect Business Value and Technical Complexity to declare matrix quadrant.
substeps.input:
- Business Value: HIGH (Step 1).
- Technical Complexity: MEDIUM (Step 2).
substeps.raw_data: High Value / Low Complexity: Quick Win. High Value / Medium-High Complexity: Strategic Initiative. Low Value / Low Complexity: Fill-in. Low Value / High Complexity: Money Pit.

micro.title: Matrix intersection and quadrant declaration
micro.objective: Declare matrix quadrant from intersection of HIGH Value and MEDIUM Complexity.

steps: Plot coordinates: X = Medium Complexity, Y = High Value.
Locate intersection: Strategic Initiative quadrant.
Formulate quadrant interpretation: worthwhile investment requiring structured architectural design in Phase 5.
how_to.table_columns: Value Axis | Complexity Axis | Resulting Quadrant | Project Classification
restrictions: Strategic Initiative is not a casual quick win; demands dedicated design.

micro.example:
| Value Axis | Complexity Axis | Resulting Quadrant | Project Classification |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **HIGH** | **MEDIUM** | **`Strategic Initiative`** | High-impact project; justifies dedicated architectural design (Phase 5) rather than a hasty afternoon patch. |

substeps.title: Human Confirmation (Context Reviewer)
substeps.objective: Audit sources and obtain Project Authority signature to prevent analyst bias.
substeps.input:
- Matrix intersection results.
- Stakeholder roles from D6.
substeps.raw_data: Context Reviewer: Carlos Ruiz (Operations Coordinator). Project Authority: Laura Torres (Sponsor / Property Owner).

micro.title: Reviewer audit
micro.objective: A second person with operational context verifies that all cells cite concrete evidence rather than subjective impressions.

steps: Reviewer Carlos Ruiz inspects Value cell: verified against Criterion C and 9,600,000 COP figure in D3.
Reviewer inspects Complexity cell: verified against literal D2 Technical Focus.
Confirm zero unsourced personal impressions.
Issue Reviewer Audit Finding: NO REMARKS / APPROVED.

how_to.table_rules: Rows verifying source compliance for each matrix dimension.
restrictions: Reviewer must not be the author of the matrix.
Every cell must cite an E-XX or master criterion.

substeps.title: Continuity Signal (not cancellation)
substeps.objective: Issue the formal continuity signal based on matrix quadrant.

Forward signal to D5 (Objectives) and D7 (Risks) to maintain normal Phase 0 workflow.

- **Technical Complexity (High/Medium/Low):** MEDIUM — *Justification: concurrency control with standard transactional patterns, without integrations or hardware (D2 Technical Focus).*

### 3. Matrix Placement

- **Continuity Signal:** PRIORITIZE (no Low Priority Alert activated).
